excerpt: An expat's guide to buying Abu Dhabi property: investment-area eligibility, documents, registration, payment and ongoing ownership costs.
introduction:
An expat buying property in Abu Dhabi should first confirm the right available for the exact property, then verify the seller or developer, transaction documents and full cost. Abu Dhabi's rules provide for non-national ownership in investment areas, but the status and nature of an individual right must be checked with the relevant authority.

This guide follows official Abu Dhabi Real Estate Centre (ADREC) and DARI information checked on 8 November 2026. Confirm current requirements and charges for your own transaction before paying.
takeaways: Confirm the property's investment-area status and the right available to the buyer with ADREC or the relevant registrar.
Verify title or initial registration, seller authority, mortgage, tenancy and any required clearance.
Obtain a written cost and payment schedule and retain the official registration outcome.

sections.heading: Where can an expat own property?
sections.body:
ADREC's [registration legislation](https://adrec.gov.ae/en/rules_and_regulations/registration) includes amended provisions allowing non-national individuals and legal persons to acquire real rights in properties located in investment areas. Ask the authority to confirm the investment-area status, type of right and any conditions for the exact unit and buyer.

Do not assume every Abu Dhabi property offers the same right. Request the project and unit number, title or initial registration and the seller's authority. If buying through a company or a representative, ask what additional documents and eligibility conditions apply.

The [Abu Dhabi area guide](/journal/abu-dhabi-real-estate-2026) provides location context; it does not establish the legal status of a particular property.

sections.heading: Compare ready and off-plan documents
sections.body:
For a ready home, inspect the actual unit and common areas. Review the title, seller identity, any mortgage, existing lease and service-charge statement. Confirm when possession can be given and which clearance is required. A property can be complete yet still be occupied.

For off-plan, verify the registered project and developer, signed plan, specification, payment recipient, instalments and handover terms. Ask how the sale is initially registered and obtain evidence identifying the buyer and unit. Check the contract's delay, default and cancellation provisions with a qualified adviser if needed.

Do not rely on a rendering, verbal assurance or reservation receipt as proof of a registered ownership right. Keep contracts, receipts and correspondence together.

sections.heading: What does registration involve?
sections.body:
DARI's [sale and purchase registration service](https://services.dari.ae/consumer-services/registration-of-sale-and-purchase-of-land-and-real-estate/) describes submitting an application, documents and fees and receiving a title deed for the stated service. Its page lists a 2% registration fee on contract value and an AED 875 electronic service fee, with additional mortgage-related items where applicable. Confirm current applicability and the payer for your case.

ADREC's legislation describes a sale fee shared equally between seller and buyer unless otherwise agreed, within the framework stated there. The contract and current service quote determine the allocation; do not assume the buyer always pays the full transaction fee.

Ask which identification, agreement, valuation and representation documents are required. Verify payment instructions independently and check the issued document's names and unit details.

sections.heading: Plan the cash and financing
sections.body:
Add the agreed price, buyer-paid registration and service fees, brokerage, lender charges, insurance, inspection and initial work. Keep a separate reserve. If borrowing, request the bank's valuation, loan amount, rate, fees and repayment schedule; approval depends on the borrower and property.

For illustration, a sample buyer pays AED 1,000,000 for a property and assumes AED 50,000 of combined transaction and setup costs. The total is AED 1,050,000 before a separate reserve. The example allocation shows one approach; use the payment terms set out in your signed agreement.

The chart shows the components. The [Abu Dhabi purchase cost guide](/journal/total-cost-of-buying-an-apartment-in-abu-dhabi) explains how to build a unit-specific budget.

A written financing offer should also show the lender’s valuation and the date by which the funds are expected to be released.

sections.heading: Check ongoing costs and intended use
sections.body:
Request the current service-charge statement, management contact, maintenance history and any arrears. Include insurance, utilities and repairs in the annual budget. If the apartment will be rented, allow for vacancy, management and comparable lease evidence.

Check any lender restrictions and the applicable tenancy registration procedure. Compare projected yield with signed leases, owner costs and resale evidence. For a family home, test the school and work routes from the actual building and confirm admission or transport with providers.

A property purchase, mortgage approval and residence visa are separate decisions. Verify each with the responsible institution rather than assuming one automatically grants another.

sections.heading: Prepare for a non-resident or representative purchase
sections.body:
If you are outside the UAE or appoint someone to act for you, ask the registrar and bank what identification, power of attorney, notarisation, attestation and translation are required. Confirm the representative's authority and use independently verified contact details for payments.

Consider cross-border tax and reporting obligations with an appropriately qualified adviser. Allow time for bank checks, currency conversion and transfer, and retain documentation of the source and destination of funds. Requirements depend on your circumstances and the service used.

Ask how you will receive registration documents and notices after completion and how the building manager will contact you. If an agent will manage a rental, set written limits for repair approvals and require regular statements. Keep copies of the title, agreement and payments accessible to your authorised representative.

sections.heading: Request a current shortlist
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Abu Dhabi project collection](/projects?emirate=Abu%20Dhabi) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your nationality, budget and intended use. Ask which exact units are currently available and request their documents and written terms for careful review.

Confirm the ownership right and current official process before committing.
